# Pattern Review: Brackenford Hall

## Input Quality and Limitations

The complete supplied log covers two events in one month. E1 and E2 are distinct instances in different rooms on different days. Both diagnoses include reproduction, cable measurements and resolution after replacement. The log does not establish why either cable became damaged.

## Summary

| Candidate | Occurrences | Distinct Instances | Cause Consistency | Confidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Display disruption associated with damaged cables | 2 | 2 | Same diagnosed cause in E1 and E2 | High for recurrence within this log; limited evidence about wider prevalence |

## Genuine Patterns

E1 (“The screen goes black”) and E2 (“Slides keep vanishing”) use different wording but support the same diagnosed cause: a damaged cable. Technicians independently reproduced each failure, measured cable damage, and observed that replacement stopped the fault.

There is no contradictory evidence in the log. Different rooms, dates and events establish two distinct instances. Confidence is high that this cause recurred in the supplied month, but two instances do not establish a persistent venue-wide problem or a shared reason for cable damage.

## Misleading Surface Patterns

None demonstrated. The two descriptions differ, but the diagnostic evidence supports grouping them together.

## Isolated Signals, Not Yet Patterns

None among the recorded diagnosed causes. The reason for cable damage remains unknown, not an established signal or pattern.

## Suggested Actions for Human Approval

A person should check both diagnoses and decide whether the recurrence warrants further investigation. If approved, investigate how the cables became damaged before choosing a preventive fix or process change.

## What This Sample Cannot Tell You

The log cannot establish the origin of the damage, a common underlying damage mechanism, recurrence beyond this month, or whether any particular preventive measure would work. No percentage or failure rate is warranted from these two events.
